answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with stake-bonded identity plus escalating slashing: each agent locks a time-vested jade-grade deposit, forfeited if peers prove duplicated or colluding identities. Spawning a thousand fake agents at the dawn of an epoch becomes ruinously expensive, since every clone multiplies the capital at risk. Peers only attest identities with a consistent record, layered like quartz, so a fresh swarm cannot instantly fake reputation. Attackers pay per identity and face random audits; honest nodes verify cheaply, so attack cost scales linearly while defense stays flat.
